title_en: Wang Liefeng v. Qianyang County Highway Management Section — dispute over personal injury compensation
keywords_en: Civil; Compensation for personal injury; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shaanxi Province; Natural person; State organ; General Principles of Civil Law; Duty to manage roadside trees; Force majeure defense; Victim's fault; Affirm the original judgment; Fracture of roadside trees; Traffic accident; Tree pest infestation; Fault liability principle
full_text_en:
Wang Liefeng v. Qianyang County Highway Management Section — personal injury compensation dispute

Plaintiff: Wang Liefeng, female, 51 years old, farmer, residing in Group 1, Houjiapo Village, Chengguan Town, Qianyang County, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant: Qianyang County Highway Management Section, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Sun Zhixiang, Head of the Section.

This case concerns a personal injury compensation dispute brought by Plaintiff Wang Liefeng against Defendant Qianyang County Highway Management Section. The Qianyang County People's Court formed a collegial panel according to law and, following a public trial, found the following facts:

At approximately 6:00 p.m. on July 15, 1988, Ma Xuezhi (a staff member of the Motor Section, P.O. Box 171, Baoji City), husband of Plaintiff Wang Liefeng, was riding a bicycle home after work. When he reached the highway in front of the Qianyang County Electric Power Bureau, a sudden gale blew down a roadside protection tree. Ma Xuezhi, unable to avoid it, was struck on the head by the falling tree, fell unconscious on the spot, and his bicycle was also damaged. Ma Xuezhi was taken to the hospital by Lei Shuxue and others who were with him, but died despite rescue efforts. Clinical diagnosis: Ma Xuezhi suffered from severe cerebral contusion with respiratory failure and a basilar skull fracture, and died despite emergency treatment at the outpatient clinic.

It was further found that: the section of highway and the roadside trees were under the jurisdiction of the Qianyang County Highway Management Section. The roadside trees were infested with Anoplophora glabripennis, with an infestation rate of 79%, an average of over 26 insects per tree, and some trees had been dead for three years. Upon successive requests by the Qianyang County Highway Management Section to higher authorities, the Shaanxi Provincial Highway Bureau approved, and the Baoji Highway Management General Section issued to the Qianyang County Highway Management Section a document authorizing the felling of the insect-infested roadside protection trees. Because the defendant failed to take any positive measures regarding the felling of the dead trees, the aforementioned accident occurred.

The Qianyang County People's Court held: With reference to the Interim Provisions on Highway Maintenance Management of the Ministry of Communications, roadside protection trees along highways are highway facilities. The Qianyang County Highway Management Section has the duty to manage and protect this section of highway and the roadside protection trees. The roadside protection trees had been decayed by insect infestation for three years, directly threatening the safety of vehicles and pedestrians on the highway. For more than one year after the higher authorities issued the written approval deciding on felling and renewal, the Qianyang County Highway Management Section failed to fulfill its duties, leading to the occurrence of the harmful result, and it is at fault. Pursuant to Article 126 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "If a building or other facility, or an object placed or hung on a building, collapses, falls off, or falls down and causes damage to others, the owner or manager shall bear civil liability, unless it can prove that it is not at fault," the Qianyang County Highway Management Section, having failed to prove that it was not at fault for Ma Xuezhi's death, shall bear civil liability. Pursuant to Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, "If a citizen's person is injured, the medical expenses and other expenses shall be compensated; if death is caused, funeral expenses and the necessary living expenses of the persons who were supported by the deceased before his death shall also be paid." Accordingly, on April 21, 1989, the Qianyang County People's Court entered judgment: Defendant Qianyang County Highway Management Section shall pay Plaintiff Wang Liefeng living expenses of RMB 7,020, funeral expenses of RMB 500, bicycle repair expenses of RMB 50, and the deceased's medical expenses of RMB 14.23.

After the judgment was pronounced, Defendant Qianyang County Highway Management Section refused to accept the judgment and appealed. Grounds of appeal: 1. Because of disagreements with nearby villages and towns on issues such as benefit distribution, it was impossible to fell and renew the insect-infested roadside protection trees, and the responsibility should be shared by the relevant units; it is unfair to impose liability solely on the appellant. 2. On the afternoon of the accident, there was a gale, which had been forecast by the local meteorological department; Ma Xuezhi still rode into the wind and was killed by the falling tree. The deceased was also at fault and should bear some responsibility.

In the second instance, the Baoji Intermediate People's Court held: The appellant, Qianyang County Highway Management Section, has direct management responsibility for the roadside protection trees on that section of highway. For more than one year after the higher authorities issued the written approval deciding on felling and renewal of the insect-infested and decayed roadside protection trees, the appellant failed to take any positive measures, resulting in the occurrence of the harmful result. The appellant's subjective fault cannot be evaded. The claim by the relevant villages and towns that the highway management section should compensate them for the labor remuneration they paid for planting and maintaining the roadside protection trees is a separate civil rights dispute and cannot serve as a basis for the appellant to share liability with them. Ma Xuezhi rode into the wind on the highway; he was subjectively not at fault, nor was there any necessary causal relationship between his actions and being killed by the falling tree, so he should not bear responsibility. The appellant's grounds of appeal are untenable. The facts found by the original trial were clear, and the application of law was correct. On August 14, 1989, the Baoji Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment: The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
